items.q: What does he mean by lowering the bar?
items.a: The first moment costs more than the task. Put on the shoes, open the document, drink one glass of water. Five minutes, and you are allowed to stop. The brain resists starting, not continuing.

items.q: Why a ritual instead of a routine?
items.a: A routine still needs willpower, and some days that is already gone. A ritual is the same cue every time: music, a candle, jazz at the door, the mat already out. You are Pavlov's dog.

items.q: What is the hundred people image?
items.a: You would not let a hundred people into the bedroom before you washed your face. The phone lets them into the bedroom of your mind. The algorithm's job is to keep you glued, not to make you happy.
Distance, not a stronger resolve. Phone in another room. Delete the apps for a day, not the accounts. No phone for the first hour and the last hour.
Nothing. No phone, music, book, or TV. Day one is uncomfortable. By the end of the week he says the ideas show up. Cheap hits feel good first and like poison after. Replace them.
Three minutes. Three things you did right. The traffic jam sticks and the smooth drive does not, so you have to write the win down.
